rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Three empirical laws anchor gas behaviour: **Boyle** ($PV$ = const at fixed T), **Charles** ($V/T$ = const at fixed P) and the **pressure law** ($P/T$ = const at fixed V). Combined for a fixed amount of gas they give $P_1V_1/T_1 = P_2V_2/T_2$, and with amount included the **ideal gas equation** $PV = nRT$ (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹K⁻¹) or, per molecule, $PV = Nk_BT$.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - PV = nRT; PV = Nk_BT - P₁V₁/T₁ = P₂V₂/T₂ - R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹K⁻¹; k_B = R/N_A = 1.38×10⁻²³ J/K

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Ideal Gas Assumptions:** The equation $PV = nRT$ assumes (1) molecules are point particles with zero volume, (2) no intermolecular forces except during elastic collisions, (3) motion is random and obeys Newton's laws. These hold best at high temperature and low pressure; real gases deviate near condensation.  ·  **Universal Gas Constant:** $R = 8.314 ext{ J/mol·K}$ is the same for all ideal gases. It connects macroscopic ($P, V, n, T$) to microscopic ($k_B, N_A$) via $R = N_A k_B$. The value depends on units: $R = 0.0821 ext{ L·atm/mol·K}$ in common chemistry units.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Never substitute Celsius into PV=nRT.  ·  Gauge pressure is not absolute pressure.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: **Kelvin, always:** gas laws die at 0 °C input — convert T + 273 first.  ·  **n vs N:** n = moles (use R); N = molecules (use k_B).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: A 2 mol gas occupies 0.050 m³ at 300 K. Find absolute pressure.  ·  A gas at 100 kPa and 300 K is heated to 360 K at fixed volume. Find final pressure.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (3m): A tyre is inflated to 2 atm at 17 °C. What is its pressure at 47 °C (volume constant)?** — P₂ = P₁T₂/T₁ = 2 × 320/290 = 2.21 atm.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: The 2024 3m asks for all three laws plus the combination — write each formula first.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **The combined-gas shortcut:** P₁V₁/T₁ = P₂V₂/T₂ solves most numericals without finding n.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: PV = nRT; R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹K⁻¹; PV = Nk_BT.  ·  Boyle (T): PV const; Charles (P): V/T const; pressure law (V): P/T const.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: At STP one mole of any ideal gas occupies 22.4 L — Avogadro's hypothesis in numbers.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Gas Laws Combined Boyle, Charles and Gay-Lussac each froze one variable and watched two others. Combine their three laws and out falls PV = nRT — one equation that predicts the pressure, volume or temperature of any (ideal) gas from the other two plus the amount of gas.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2022, 2024) ### 2.1 The three empirical laws | Law | Statement | Formula (constant) | |---|---|---| | **Boyle's law** | At constant T, pressure ∝ 1/volume | $PV = $ const (T, n fixed) | | **Charles's law** | At constant P, volume ∝ absolute temperature | $V/T = $ const (P, n fixed) | | **Pressure (Gay-Lussac) law** | At constant V, pressure ∝…  ·  ## 3. Conceptual Relationships - **To Topic 63/64:** kinetic theory derives PV = ⅓Nmv̄² and matches it to PV = NkT — the microscopic origin of the gas laws. - **To real gases:** the equation holds only at low pressure and high temperature; real gases need van der Waals corrections. - **To Avogadro:** equal volumes of gases at same T, P contain equal numbers of molecules.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Temperature Must Be Absolute:** $T$ must be in Kelvin for $PV = nRT$ to hold. Using Celsius gives incorrect results because $T=0^\circ ext{C} eq 0$ kinetic energy. The linear proportionality $P \propto T$ and $V \propto T$ only works with absolute temperature.  ·  Verified PYQs: laws + combination 2024 3m; P = nRT/V 2024 2m; Charles numerical 2022 4m.  ·  "The ideal gas equation combines Boyle's, Charles's and the pressure law: PV = nRT."
